deals.travelWindow: Aug 24 – Sep 2, cheapest one-stop (Frontier); nonstop AA/United/JetBlue run closer to $220
deals.whyRanked: The cheapest verified fare of the five at $166 RT, and Indiana Dunes National Park is about an hour away by car or the South Shore Line train.
deals.soloWhy: The Loop and Riverwalk are dense, walkable, and connected by the L, so a car is never needed to explore solo.

highlights: Chicago Riverwalk architecture boat cruise
Millennium Park and Cloud Gate ("The Bean")
Art Institute of Chicago
Indiana Dunes National Park day trip via the South Shore Line
Wicker Park / Logan Square for vintage shops and coffee
itinerary: Day 1 — Land, walk the Riverwalk, take a 90-minute architecture river cruise, dinner in the West Loop.
Day 2 — Millennium Park and the Art Institute in the morning, Wicker Park/Logan Square in the afternoon, deep-dish dinner.
Day 3 — South Shore Line train to Indiana Dunes National Park, hike the West Beach or Mount Baldy trail, back to Chicago, fly home.
guide.gettingAround: The L and Riverwalk make downtown, the Loop, and the Near North Side fully walkable/transit-friendly; skip a rental car unless doing the Indiana Dunes day trip, which is also reachable by train.
guide.stayArea: The Loop or West Loop — walkable, near transit, close to restaurants.

deals.whyRanked: $188 RT nonstop, and De Soto National Memorial plus the Gulf beaches are under an hour away for a nature break without leaving the Tampa Bay area.
deals.soloWhy: Downtown's Riverwalk is compact and walkable for an evening, but the beaches and De Soto Memorial call for a rental car.

highlights: Tampa Riverwalk and Curtis Hixon Waterfront Park
Ybor City historic cigar district and nightlife
Tampa Museum of Art
De Soto National Memorial day trip
Sunset at St. Pete or Clearwater Beach
itinerary: Day 1 — Land, walk the Riverwalk, Tampa Museum of Art, dinner in Ybor City.
Day 2 — Drive to De Soto National Memorial and the Bradenton-area beaches, or stay closer and walk St. Pete's Central Avenue.
Day 3 — Ybor City cigar-rolling demo and Centro Ybor, sunset at Clearwater Beach, fly home.
guide.gettingAround: Downtown Riverwalk and Ybor City are walkable; a rental car is worth it for De Soto National Memorial or the Gulf beaches, 30–50 minutes away.
guide.stayArea: Downtown/Riverwalk — walkable, close to restaurants, easy highway access for day trips.

deals.whyRanked: $222 RT nonstop, and Rocky Mountain National Park is about 90 minutes away via Estes Park — one of the most accessible major national parks from any big-city airport.
deals.soloWhy: LoDo and the 16th Street corridor are walkable and reachable from the airport via the A Line train, and Denver's outdoor-gear/hostel scene makes linking up for day hikes easy solo.

highlights: LoDo and Larimer Square
Denver Art Museum
Red Rocks Park & Amphitheatre
Rocky Mountain NP day trip via the Bear Lake corridor
REI flagship store and Confluence Park
itinerary: Day 1 — A Line train into LoDo, walk Larimer Square, dinner and a brewery in RiNo.
Day 2 — Drive to Rocky Mountain NP via Estes Park, hike Bear Lake to Nymph and Dream Lake (easy 2.2 mi RT), push on to Emerald Lake if energy allows.
Day 3 — Red Rocks Park in the morning, Denver Art Museum or Confluence Park, fly home.
guide.gettingAround: The A Line train covers DEN-to-downtown; rent a car only for the Rocky Mountain NP day (a timed-entry reservation is needed in peak season).
guide.stayArea: LoDo or RiNo — walkable, close to breweries and the train line.

deals.whyRanked: $228 RT nonstop, French Quarter walkability is hard to beat for a solo trip, and the Barataria Preserve unit of Jean Lafitte National Historical Park is a half-hour away.
deals.soloWhy: The French Quarter and Faubourg Marigny are dense, walkable, and full of live music where striking up a conversation solo at the bar is the norm.

highlights: French Quarter walk — Jackson Square, Royal Street galleries
St. Louis Cathedral
Frenchmen Street live music
Barataria Preserve boardwalk trail (alligators, cypress swamp)
Garden District streetcar ride
itinerary: Day 1 — Walk the French Quarter: Jackson Square, Royal Street, beignets at Café du Monde, Frenchmen Street for live music at night.
Day 2 — Barataria Preserve boardwalk trail in the morning (30-minute drive, or book a guided swamp tour), Garden District streetcar ride and Lafayette Cemetery in the afternoon.
Day 3 — Frenchmen Art Market, po'boy lunch, fly home.
guide.gettingAround: The French Quarter, Marigny, and Garden District (via the St. Charles streetcar) don't require a car; rent one only for the Barataria Preserve day, or book a swamp tour instead.
guide.stayArea: French Quarter or Faubourg Marigny — walkable, central, close to music venues.

deals.whyRanked: $240 RT nonstop, and the historic peninsula is one of the most walkable downtowns in the South, with Francis Marion National Forest under an hour away.
deals.soloWhy: The historic peninsula is flat, compact, and safe to wander alone — cobblestone streets, the Battery, and the City Market are all within walking distance of most downtown hotels.

highlights: Rainbow Row and the Battery waterfront walk
Charleston City Market
Fort Sumter National Monument ferry
Angel Oak Tree on Johns Island
Francis Marion National Forest day trip
itinerary: Day 1 — Walk the Battery and Rainbow Row, Charleston City Market, dinner downtown.
Day 2 — Ferry to Fort Sumter National Monument in the morning, Angel Oak Tree on Johns Island in the afternoon.
Day 3 — Drive to Francis Marion National Forest for a short hike or paddle at the Sewee Visitor Center, fly home.
guide.gettingAround: Downtown is entirely walkable or a short pedicab/bike ride; rent a car (or book a tour) only for Johns Island or the national forest.
guide.stayArea: Downtown peninsula — walkable, near restaurants and the waterfront.
